None of the eight qualified, so no entry carries the field. `surface` is a third, separate reading, and each one names its own source: the published @wordpress/components 41.0.0 and @wordpress/ui 0.23.0 packages, read 2026-10-02.
note: Component currency, not props -- plus, where an entry carries `surface`, what the component styles itself on the element its `className` reaches, and the prop that controls each property (`null`: it sets it and no prop does). `system/override` blocks only on a property a surface lists; an entry with no `surface` has not been read for one, so a class on it is treated like a class on a plain element. `"properties": {}` is a verified answer -- it owns nothing there -- not a missing one. `status` says whether a component is the current best-practice choice: `recommended` (use it), `legacy` (works, but a recommended replacement now covers the job -- see `supersededBy`), `locked` (a private API Gutenberg explicitly does not recommend outside core -- can break without notice on any update), `experimental` (real, documented, but WordPress's own Storybook metadata (`componentStatus.status: 'use-with-caution'`) flags it not-yet-safe to mix with @wordpress/components -- true of almost every real WP admin codebase today, so treat as informational, not a migration target, until that gate lifts). Two components can share a name across packages with different status -- `Button` in `@wordpress/components` is `recommended` today while the newer `Button` in `@wordpress/ui` is `experimental`; check `package` too. This file is the canonical answer to 'is this the current best practice' -- the design-system MCP is for prop/usage detail on a component you've already chosen, and does not carry this maturity signal at all (it presents `experimental`-status components with the same confidence as `recommended` ones, and is itself measurably behind trunk for several @wordpress/ui additions: Dialog, AlertDialog, Drawer, IconButton, LinkButton, and the current Menu all return nothing from `get_component_details`). Re-verify against trunk (`packages/ui/src/*/stories/index.story.tsx` -> `parameters.componentStatus`) before bumping this file's version -- do not guess a status. `dropIn` is a much narrower claim than `status`: that moving the import changes the specifier and nothing else. A matching name is not evidence for it -- see docs/design/checks.md#a-same-name-move-is-not-a-drop-in-move.

variants.heading-2xl: Page title. 32px, semibold. One per screen, at the top.
variants.heading-md: Subsection title or group label. 13px, semibold: body size, set apart only by weight.
variants.heading-sm: Small overline or eyebrow label above a group. 11px, semibold.
variants.body-xl: Large lead or display copy. 20px, regular.
variants.body-md: Default body text: paragraphs, labels, values. 13px, regular.
variants.body-sm: Secondary text: help text, descriptions, captions, metadata, muted notes. 12px, regular.

surface.note: `className` lands on the rendered element. `variant` is the only styling prop. Colour, letter-spacing and text-transform are set by no prop -- only `heading-sm` also sets `text-transform: uppercase` -- so a class setting them is the sanctioned channel. Rendered as h1-h6, an unlayered defense rule (`:is(h1, ..., h6).heading`, specificity 0,1,1) sets `color`, so a one-class colour rule loses to it there; the preset sanctions colour through `style` instead.
